title: Please make more VR games!
author: albatrossalt
selftext: Everyone is posting these great looking games, claude and astra can basically make anything in Blender. Why is nobody making VR games? I have this oculus/meta quest that was such a cool idea and felt so vibrant when it came out, but there has been nothing cool released for it since Half Life Alyx. It just sits there collecting dust. Please somebody use your vibe coding skills for good and give us some awesome new VR games.

replies.body: Something like subnautica that actually works in VR would be sweet (i know they say that support it but it is really poorly implemented). Anything like exploring a new place. Or more escape room games. Just not sorting nails or finding needles in bales of hay plz :')

comments.author: unfamily_friendly
comments.body:
VR market has 3 people worldwide, and I don't remember the last time i player my Quest 3. Players don't have expectations from VR market, as most releases are pretty shitty. Devs not trying
 make a second boneworks or HLA. They try to make a second Beat Saber. The only promising games on a market are backed by Patreon supporters and will be forever in alpha. And even if you do make your very immersive VR masterpiece (which is extremely easy today) - the game will not sell well

replies.author: M4xs0n
replies.body: That’s the issue. But it’s actually easy af to make a VR mod today. Depends on the polishing you want for your own game, but devs should focus on making awesome flatscreen game first and then port it over to VR with AI. That’s the best out of both worlds

comments.author: redditscraperbot2
comments.body:
\>Why is nobody making VR games?

Not many people have VR headsets to justify the time investment to potential payoff.

replies.author: tomqmasters
replies.body: But there are also fewer VR games to compete with and people will pay $20+ for a game that's relatively simple to make.

comments.author: NoName847
comments.body:
I think the VR space will be one of the most impacted , there are really zero devs left that make anything , but still millions of fans with headsets looking for games me included

If we consumers can start making our own games and it isnt a crippling multi year grind to get there , it might just revive the space entirely 

in contrast PC never had a problem of getting too little releases , VR players have been starving for years

comments.author: ImportGuy
comments.body: Honest question because I’d be down to work on the this, what kind of games sound appealing? Like what would you play that you can’t already get on the Quest?

replies.author: gefahr
replies.body:
Yup. I think people just don't realize how many orders of magnitude are between each of those. Mobile to PC to VR, it'd be like that size comparison of the sun earth and moon.

Doesn't matter if there's less competition if the total market size isn't enough to make it worthwhile.

Would be very curious what the gross of the best-selling VR games is.

comments.author: Maksitaxi
comments.body:
I make ai vr games and the main problem is that we don't have an vr ai director. so the games is much harder to make than ordindary games. 

For now i think our best use of ai is to make vr mods for games already made.

comments.author: Skazmodan
comments.body:
Actually I am planning around with opus5.5 and unity mcp to build a VR experience for myself and my friends as an experiment.  
Concept is a social first car ride down a beautiful path in a self driving car while playing music.  
Its to relive the old days when friends lived in the same city before jobs took us all to far cities.   
I got core mechanics working but the art style is garbage atm lol.

comments.author: SmoggySPECTEREGaming
comments.body:
I am making a VR RPG called Elyndor: Shards of Aether. I am about 6 months into the project, but am working toward finishing my first vertical slice. A quick sneak peak:

- A diegetic Journal UI
- your traditional "bars" will be a module on your gauntlet.
- gesture based magic systems and a customizable "spell selector" on your runic gauntlet.
- melee, archery and magic combat.
- dungeons
- bosses 
- quests
- collectibles like Mounts and pets

Likely to take several years even with the help of AI. Developing in VR with XR interactable is venuine hardmode compared to a one shot prompt for a cookie cutter game. It's also my first experience ever in game development so I am learning on the fly. That said, it will release one day, and when it does, I hope you like it.
